text: In the coherent type-1 feed-forward loop (C1-FFL), X activates Y, X activates Z, and Y also activates Z (AND logic at Z). What dynamical behavior does this topology produce?
choices: A transient pulse of Z expression that decays back to baseline even while X remains present, detecting fold-change in X
Bistability with hysteresis between two alternative stable expression states of Z
Perfect adaptation of Z to a persistent level of X, via integral feedback control
A sign-sensitive delay: activation of Z is delayed until the X signal is sustained, filtering out brief ON pulses, while deactivation of Z is fast
explanation: The C1-FFL is the classic 'sign-sensitive delay' motif: because both the direct path (X to Z) and indirect path (X to Y to Z) must be active to turn Z on, a brief pulse of X does not give Y time to accumulate, filtering transient noise; loss of X removes activation immediately, so OFF-switching is fast. Choice 0 describes the incoherent type-1 FFL, not the coherent type. Choice 1 describes positive feedback loops, and choice 2 describes an adaptation circuit such as E. coli chemotaxis -- neither is a property of feed-forward loops.
